faq.q: Will the ingredients and nutrition label stay accurate?
faq.a: The main label follows your photo, but small text can blur. Keep ingredients, allergens, and nutrition facts in your listing and check the label before posting.

faq.q: Can I make a drink look cold without a photo shoot?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear bottle photo and ask for condensation or ice in the scene. Check that the finished drink still looks like yours.

faq.q: Can a drink ad have a voice and captions in another language?
faq.a: Yes. Add a voice and captions, then make another version in the language your customers speak. You can reuse the same product photo.

faq.q: Do I need a creator or filming kitchen?
faq.a: No. You can make food and drink videos from product photos with an AI actor or hands in the scene. A real tasting still needs a person.

faq.q: Can I turn a food or drink photo into a video?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear product photo or paste its link, then describe the pour, bite, or serving you want. Make a short video without a kitchen shoot.

faq.q: What should I check on the package in my video?
faq.a: Check that the package shape, color, and main label match your real product. Do not show a flavor or ingredient you do not sell.

faq.q: Which video sizes can I use for food ads?
faq.a: Choose 9:16 for TikTok and Reels, 1:1 for feeds, or 16:9 for wide placements. You can also choose 4:3 or 3:4.

faq.q: How long can a food video be, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. A product photo costs 24 credits, and failed jobs return credits.

faq.q: Can I use food and drink videos in paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Download videos without a watermark and use them in paid ads. Check that the product and any food claims match what you sell.
